name: Congenital Factor XII Deficiency

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Laboratory-based diagnosis of Factor XII deficiency

criteria.description: Markedly prolonged activated partial thromboplastin time (aPTT) with normal prothrombin time (PT)
Reduced or absent Factor XII activity confirmed by coagulation factor assay
Exclusion of other coagulation factor deficiencies and inhibitors
Identification of pathogenic mutations in the F12 gene

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Prolonged aPTT with normal PT plus reduced Factor XII activity on assay, excluding other causes
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Factor XII deficiency is typically asymptomatic and discovered incidentally during coagulation testing.

laboratory: Prolonged activated partial thromboplastin time (aPTT) with normal prothrombin time (PT)
Reduced or absent Factor XII activity on coagulation factor assay
other: No clinical bleeding despite coagulation abnormalities
Possible association with thrombotic events in some patients

distinguishingFeatures: Factor VIII deficiency causes hemophilia A with bleeding tendency
Prolonged aPTT but with clinical bleeding symptoms
Factor IX deficiency causes hemophilia B with bleeding tendency
Prolonged aPTT due to inhibitor rather than deficiency
Associated with thrombosis rather than bleeding

redFlags: Unexpected prolonged aPTT without bleeding symptoms
History of unexplained thrombosis despite coagulation abnormalities
Recurrent pregnancy loss with coagulation abnormalities
references: Mannucci PM. Factor XII deficiency: clinical and laboratory features. Haemophilia. 2004;10(5): 453-459.
Lippi G, Franchini M. Factor XII deficiency: a clinical perspective. Semin Thromb Hemost. 2011;37(7): 757-763.
